archetypes.name: contract-drift
archetypes.rationale: The plan changes driver stdout/stderr and exit-code contracts while explicitly deferring adjacent orchestrator-contract work.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate whether the planned ship.py and ci_monitor.py changes preserve the documented JSON-only stdout, stderr breadcrumb, and routing exit-code contracts across the files in scope. Check for missing updates to tests, docs, or constants that would leave consumers expecting the old traceback or silent behavior. Pay special attention to boundaries with the separately tracked #3446 work so the plan neither omits a necessary local contract change nor smuggles in out-of-scope orchestrator changes. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: run-log-invariants
archetypes.rationale: The plan re-architects flush behavior and volatile-log commits, which risks subtle divergence from committed run-log contracts.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare the planned run_logs.py, merge.py, and config.py changes against the repository's run-log documentation and existing tests to find gaps in the proposed volatile-only skip semantics. Verify the allowlist is planned narrowly enough to avoid dropping substantive artifacts and broadly enough to stop CI-churn commits. Look for missing contract-documentation or regression-test updates around pre-merge, post-merge, and flush-recovery behavior. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: version-floor-sync
archetypes.rationale: The plan lowers the Python runtime floor to 3.11 and must keep runtime, dev-tooling, docs, and CI claims synchronized.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the plan for all places that encode or imply the Python version floor, including runtime selectors, pyproject metadata, CI matrices, README and installation docs, and any repo instructions in scope. Distinguish runtime requirements from pre-commit or development-tooling requirements, and flag any missing evidence that the claimed 3.11 compatibility is actually tested. Check whether the proposed file list is sufficient for this version-policy change. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
